home-remodeling.hero_sub: PGX Builders Group takes 1930s-to-1950s Venetian Islands houses down to structure and rebuilds them properly: permitted in the correct city, engineered for a barrier-island site, and supervised on the island every working day.
home-remodeling.local_heading: Two cities, six islands, one contractor
intro_paragraphs: The Venetian Islands hold a century of Miami architecture on six causeway-linked islands: Mediterranean Revival villas from the original boom, Art Deco and postwar houses on Di Lido and Rivo Alto, and a growing roster of glassy new builds on the open-bay lots. Owners here rarely want a light refresh. The home remodeling projects we run on San Marino or San Marco are full-gut renovations, with new layouts, structural openings toward the water, complete electrical, plumbing, and mechanical replacement, and impact glazing throughout. Done right, that keeps a good island house standing for another fifty years.

Permitting here starts with a question many contractors get wrong: which city is your island in? Biscayne and San Marco Islands permit through the City of Miami Building Department under Miami 21 zoning. San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto, and Belle Isle answer to the City of Miami Beach, which adds design review on single-family work and some of Florida's strictest flood rules. The islands sit in FEMA flood zones, so on older homes the substantial-improvement threshold, the so-called 50 percent rule, shapes what a remodel can legally be. We model that math with you before you commit to a direction.

PGX Builders Group measures experience in inspections passed: 20-plus years in South Florida and more than 150 remodels and additions, all of them permitted. On the Venetian Islands that experience shows up as a fixed written scope before demolition starts, a supervisor on site daily, and finish protection treated as seriously as structure. One licensed team, CGC1539072, carries the project from first estimate through warranty, so there is never a subcontractor pointing at another subcontractor while your house sits open to the weather.

faqs.q: Which building department covers my Venetian Islands home?
faqs.a: It depends on your island. Biscayne Island and San Marco Island are in the City of Miami, so permits go through the City of Miami Building Department. San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto, and Belle Isle are in the City of Miami Beach and permit through its Building Department, with Miami Beach planning review layered on top. The two cities run different processes and timelines, and we manage both regularly.

faqs.q: What is the 50 percent rule and does it affect my remodel?
faqs.a: Federal flood rules say that if improvements to a home in a flood zone exceed 50 percent of the structure's market value, the entire house must be brought up to current flood elevation standards. Since most original Venetian Islands homes sit lower than today's requirements, a large remodel can cross that line. We evaluate your project against the threshold early, so the design is built around the rule instead of colliding with it mid-permit.

faqs.q: Should I remodel my island house or tear it down and rebuild?
faqs.a: Honest answer: it depends on the structure and what you want from it. A sound 1930s or 1950s house with good bones and a workable footprint often rewards a deep remodel, and keeps character new construction cannot buy. A compromised structure, or a program that needs full current flood elevation, can argue for rebuilding. We walk the house, review the numbers both ways, and tell you which project we would build if it were ours.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-home remodel take on the Venetian Islands?
faqs.a: Plan in phases: design and engineering, then permitting through either Miami or Miami Beach, then construction. Permitting on a full-gut remodel is measured in months, not weeks, in both cities, and construction on a substantial island home typically runs the better part of a year or more depending on scope. We give you a schedule in writing with the fixed scope, and we flag the long-lead items, like windows and custom millwork, on day one.

faqs.q: What does a high-end whole-home remodel cost here?
faqs.a: There is no honest single number; scope, structure, and finish level move the total enormously. What we can say: Venetian Islands projects are built to a waterfront standard, with impact glazing, engineered structure, and premium finishes, and budgets should be set accordingly. PGX is not the cheap bid and does not pretend to be. We price a fixed written scope in real materials, so the number you approve is the number you build to.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Remodeling in the Venetian Islands, FL | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchens for Venetian Islands houses and Belle Isle condos: cabinetry, stone, and structural openings, permitted in the right city. Call (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: PGX Builders Group designs and builds custom kitchens across the Venetian Islands, licensed and permitted through Miami or Miami Beach as your island requires, and supervised daily from demolition to the last cabinet pull.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: A kitchen worthy of the water view
intro_paragraphs: The typical Venetian Islands kitchen was drawn when cooking was hidden labor: a closed room at the back of a Mediterranean villa or a midcentury ranch on Rivo Alto, San Marino, or Di Lido. Today's owners want the opposite, and a kitchen remodeling project here usually means a large working island, custom cabinetry to the ceiling, book-matched stone, and a sightline straight through the living room to Biscayne Bay. Getting there means moving walls, not just cabinets, and on this housing stock that is structural work worth doing once and doing correctly.

The permit path follows your address. Biscayne and San Marco Islands file with the City of Miami; San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto, and Belle Isle file with the City of Miami Beach. A cabinet swap is simple, but relocating gas, moving plumbing, opening a bearing wall, or enlarging a window toward the terrace each triggers its own review. In the Belle Isle towers, buildings like Nine Island Avenue, the Grand Venetian, and Costa Brava, the association's alteration approval, insurance requirements, and elevator schedule come before any city permit, and we handle that paperwork as part of the job.

Kitchens are where a fixed written scope earns its keep, because kitchens are where vague allowances go to die. PGX prices the actual cabinetry, the actual slabs, and the actual appliances before we open a wall, then supervises the site every day so your home doesn't become a staging area for unmanaged trades. We've delivered more than 150 remodels and additions across South Florida over 20-plus years, licensed and insured under CGC1539072, and every kitchen we build is permitted and inspected. No shortcuts behind the backsplash.

faqs.q: Can you open my kitchen to the living room in an older island house?
faqs.a: Usually yes, and it is the single most requested change on the Venetian Islands. Most original homes here used bearing masonry walls between kitchen and living areas, so the opening needs an engineered beam, a permit from whichever city governs your island, and inspections along the way. It is routine work for us, but it is structural work, and we treat it that way from the first sketch.

faqs.q: Do you remodel condo kitchens on Belle Isle?
faqs.a: Yes. Buildings such as Costa Brava, Belle Plaza, and the Grand Venetian each have their own alteration agreements, insurance certificate requirements, deposit rules, and elevator and work-hour schedules. We prepare the association package, coordinate with building management, and pull the City of Miami Beach permit. Tower kitchens also involve real constraints, like ventilation routing and slab penetrations, that we design around rather than discover mid-project.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel a kitchen on the islands?
faqs.a: If the work goes beyond finishes, yes. Replacing cabinets and counters in place is one thing; moving plumbing, gas, or electrical, altering walls, or changing openings requires permits, through the City of Miami for Biscayne and San Marco Islands or the City of Miami Beach for the others. Unpermitted kitchen work surfaces at appraisal or resale, and on homes at this value that is an expensive discovery. We permit everything we build.

faqs.q: How long does a custom kitchen take from start to finish?
faqs.a: The honest driver is cabinetry lead time. Fully custom millwork is typically several months from approved drawings to delivery, and permits run in parallel. Once demolition starts, a full kitchen rebuild with structural changes generally takes a few months on site. We sequence ordering so the long-lead items are in production while the permit is in review, which is how a kitchen finishes in one season instead of two.

faqs.q: What does a high-end kitchen remodel cost in this area?
faqs.a: Custom cabinetry and natural stone are the budget's center of gravity, and appliance packages at this level are their own line item. Rather than quote a misleading range, we price your actual selections in a fixed written scope, so there is a real number before demolition. Expect an investment consistent with waterfront Miami Beach homes, and expect us to tell you plainly where money buys quality and where it only buys logo.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling, Venetian Islands, Miami | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Primary-suite and condo bathroom remodels across the Venetian Islands, with waterproofing treated as structure. Licensed GC CGC1539072. Call (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: Baths built to outlast the bay
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: From primary suites on Di Lido to tower bathrooms on Belle Isle, PGX builds bathrooms that stay dry behind the stone: licensed, permitted with the correct city, and inspected at every stage.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Bathrooms for houses surrounded by water
intro_paragraphs: A surprising number of Venetian Islands bathrooms are still original to their houses: prewar tile in the Mediterranean villas, 1960s fixtures in the postwar ranches, builder-grade everything in homes flipped a decade ago. The owners who call us want a real primary suite, with a curbless shower behind frameless glass, a freestanding tub positioned for the light, honed stone, and ventilation engineered for a climate that never fully dries out. On Biscayne Island as much as Rivo Alto, that is a rebuild of the room, not a refresh, and bathroom remodeling at this level deserves to be treated like construction.

Bathroom permits follow the island: City of Miami for Biscayne and San Marco, City of Miami Beach for San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto, and Belle Isle. In the Belle Isle condominiums, buildings like Belle Plaza and Costa Brava that date to the 1960s and 70s, your renovation also runs through the association, and because towers of that era are in their milestone-inspection years, boards now read alteration requests carefully. Anything touching a plumbing riser or a slab penetration gets extra scrutiny, and frankly it should. We prepare the drawings and documentation those reviews actually ask for.

The PGX standard is that waterproofing is structure, not trim: full-membrane showers, flood-tested pans, and sealed penetrations, photographed before tile goes on so you hold proof of what's behind the marble. A fixed written scope covers fixtures down to the drain finish, a supervisor checks the site daily, and the rest of your home stays sealed off and clean while we work. Twenty-plus years in South Florida taught us exactly which details fail in this humidity, and those are the details we refuse to skip.

faqs.q: Do bathroom remodels need permits on the Venetian Islands?
faqs.a: Yes, once you move past cosmetic replacement. Relocating fixtures, altering drains, changing electrical, or reworking walls all require permits, through the City of Miami for Biscayne and San Marco Islands or the City of Miami Beach for San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto, and Belle Isle. Permitted work also means inspected waterproofing and plumbing, which on a bathroom is exactly the protection you want on record.

faqs.q: Can you renovate a bathroom in a Belle Isle condo tower?
faqs.a: Yes, and we plan them differently than house bathrooms. The association approves the alteration first, and buildings from the 1960s and 70s, now in Florida's milestone-inspection era, are rightly cautious about slab penetrations and riser tie-ins. We produce the drawings the board wants, carry the required insurance, schedule around elevator and work-hour rules, and keep the corridor cleaner than we found it. That last part matters more than people expect.

faqs.q: How do you keep a shower from leaking years later?
faqs.a: By refusing to rely on tile as waterproofing. Tile is decoration; the membrane behind it is the actual shower. We install full waterproofing membranes, flood-test pans before setting stone, seal every penetration, and photograph the assembly before it disappears behind the finish. Combined with a permitted inspection record, you get a bathroom that stays dry and documentation proving how it was built. It is the least glamorous thing we sell, and the most valuable.

faqs.q: How long does a primary bathroom remodel take?
faqs.a: A full primary suite rebuild typically runs a few months on site once permits are in hand, with stone fabrication and plumbing fixtures as the common long-lead items. Condo projects on Belle Isle add association approval time up front and work-hour limits during construction, so they run somewhat longer than the same bathroom in a house. We give you the sequence in writing before we start, and we keep to it.

faqs.q: What should I budget for a high-end bathroom here?
faqs.a: Stone, glass, and plumbing fixtures set the tone, and quality in those categories is genuinely worth paying for. Rather than throw out a number that ignores your selections, we scope the bathroom you actually want and price it fixed, in writing. Venetian Islands owners are generally investing at a level consistent with the rest of the house, and our job is to make sure the money lands in durability first and drama second.

home-additions.title: Second Stories & Additions, Venetian Islands FL | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Home additions and second stories on the Venetian Islands, engineered for dredged-fill lots, FEMA thresholds, and HVHZ wind loads. PGX Builders, (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.hero_sub: Lots on the Venetian Islands are finite. PGX adds the square footage instead: rear extensions, second stories, and reworked floor plans, engineered and permitted with the right city, supervised every working day.
home-additions.local_heading: Additions that respect the 50 percent rule
intro_paragraphs: Venetian Islands lots don't grow, and the good ones, open-bay frontage on Di Lido or skyline views off Biscayne Island, almost never trade. So owners add. A rear extension toward the seawall, a second story over a 1940s footprint, a garage converted into a gym or guest suite: these are the home additions we build here most. On houses this age the honest first step is structural, because original tie-beams, footings, and masonry need evaluation before anyone sketches new square footage. These islands are dredged fill, and the foundation story matters here more than in most of Miami.

The rules are layered. Biscayne and San Marco Islands permit additions through the City of Miami; San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto, and Belle Isle go through the City of Miami Beach, where planning review and the city's freeboard elevation requirements come into play. Everywhere on the islands, FEMA's substantial-improvement threshold hangs over older homes: cross 50 percent of the structure's value and the entire house must be brought to current flood elevation. A well-planned addition is designed around that line, or deliberately past it, with eyes open either way. We run those numbers before design money gets spent.

Additions are where PGX's habits pay off. The scope is fixed in writing, the engineering is stamped before demolition, and the connection between old and new structure, from tie-beams to roof transitions, is supervised in person rather than by phone. Deliveries get planned around the Venetian Causeway's posted bridge weight limits, so concrete pours and crane days are scheduled, not improvised. And because we've delivered 150-plus remodels and additions over 20-plus years in South Florida, we can tell you early whether your addition is a straightforward build or a negotiation with physics.

scope_items.name: Tie-beams and footings on fill

faqs.q: Can I add a second story to my Venetian Islands house?
faqs.a: Often, but the structure votes first. Original island homes were built on dredged-fill lots with foundations and tie-beams sized for one story, so we start with a structural evaluation and, where needed, soil analysis. Some houses take a second floor with targeted reinforcement; others need substantial foundation work that changes the budget conversation. Zoning height and setback limits in your island's city apply as well. We tell you which case you have before you fall in love with a rendering.

faqs.q: How does the FEMA 50 percent rule affect additions here?
faqs.a: Directly. If the total improvement exceeds 50 percent of the existing structure's market value, flood regulations require bringing the whole house to current elevation standards, which is a much bigger project than the addition alone. Because most original Venetian Islands homes sit below today's required elevations, we calculate where your project lands against the threshold at the feasibility stage and design either comfortably under it or intentionally beyond it, never accidentally across it.

faqs.q: Will my addition need design review in Miami Beach?
faqs.a: If you are on San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto, or Belle Isle, the City of Miami Beach reviews single-family additions for design compliance, much of it handled administratively by planning staff. Homes built before 1942, of which the islands have a number, can require review by the Design Review Board itself. On Biscayne and San Marco Islands, the City of Miami process applies instead. We prepare the drawings to survive whichever review your address draws.

faqs.q: Can we live in the house during an addition?
faqs.a: Frequently yes, and on the Venetian Islands most owners do. We isolate the work zone, maintain weather protection where old structure opens to new, and keep dust barriers and daily cleanup non-negotiable. There are loud phases, demolition and structural tie-in above all, and we schedule those with you in advance. If a phase would genuinely make the house unlivable, we say so before you commit rather than after the roof is open.

faqs.q: What do additions cost per square foot on the islands?
faqs.a: Per-square-foot numbers mislead on waterfront work, because foundations on fill soils, structural tie-ins, impact openings, and flood compliance vary house by house. An addition here is priced like the custom construction it is: engineered drawings, a fixed written scope, and real supplier numbers. We are a high-end builder, and our estimates reflect building to that standard, including the parts underground that no one photographs but every inspector checks.

outdoor-living.meta_description: Terraces, summer kitchens, and pool decks built for Venetian Islands waterfront lots: salt-air materials, HVHZ anchoring, permits handled. Call (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: Outdoor rooms at the water's edge
outdoor-living.hero_sub: PGX builds the outdoor half of Venetian Islands living: terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, and driveways, licensed and permitted through the correct city, engineered for wind, salt, and the occasional king tide.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Where the backyard ends at a seawall
intro_paragraphs: On the Venetian Islands the backyard is the amenity: a pool terrace facing the skyline from San Marco, dock access off Rivo Alto, long evening light on the west side of Biscayne Island. The outdoor living projects we build here are true construction, including structural pergolas, summer kitchens with gas and refrigeration, new driveways and entry sequences, and complete exterior envelope work. All of it is designed for a site that takes salt spray, full sun, and forty-knot squalls, sometimes in the same afternoon.

Exterior work is where island permitting gets layered. Your island decides the building department, City of Miami for Biscayne and San Marco, City of Miami Beach for San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto, and Belle Isle, and Miami Beach adds design review plus a seawall ordinance that sets minimum elevations for new and substantially repaired walls. Work on the seawall or dock brings Miami-Dade County environmental review into the conversation as well. Anything attached to the house or catching wind, from pergolas to shutters to doors, needs high-velocity hurricane zone product approvals. We sequence it so approvals land in the right order.

Our outdoor scopes read like our indoor ones: fixed in writing, priced in real materials such as shellstone, ipe, and marine-grade stainless, and supervised daily by people who know what salt does to the wrong hardware in a single summer. Drainage is designed rather than assumed, because low island lots forgive nothing after a rainy-season king tide. And since a project can keep us on your street for months, we run tight sites and quiet logistics; on islands this small, discretion is part of the scope. Licensed and insured, CGC1539072, 100 percent permitted work.

scope_items.name: The full skin of the house

faqs.q: Do I need permits for a pergola or summer kitchen on the islands?
faqs.a: Yes. Structures, gas lines, plumbing, and electrical all require permits through the City of Miami for Biscayne and San Marco Islands or the City of Miami Beach for the others, and anything that catches wind needs product approvals rated for Miami-Dade's high-velocity hurricane zone. An unpermitted pergola is exactly the kind of thing that surfaces during a sale or an insurance inspection. We build outdoor structures the same way we build houses: engineered, permitted, inspected.

faqs.q: Can you handle work near our seawall or dock?
faqs.a: We plan and manage it as part of the overall project. Seawall and dock work involves Miami-Dade County environmental review in addition to city permits, and on the Miami Beach islands a seawall ordinance sets minimum elevations for new and substantially repaired walls. We coordinate specialized marine contractors within a single permitted scope, so the terrace, the drainage, and the wall behave as one designed system instead of three separate projects that meet awkwardly at the property line.

faqs.q: What outdoor materials actually survive salt air?
faqs.a: Fewer than the catalogs suggest. We specify marine-grade stainless for hardware and fasteners, powder-coated aluminum or dense hardwoods like ipe for structures, and stone or porcelain surfaces that shrug off spray and sun. Standard steel fixtures and bargain hinges corrode visibly within a couple of years this close to the bay. Material selection is where an outdoor budget either protects itself or quietly evaporates, and we are opinionated about it in your favor.

faqs.q: When is the best time of year to build outdoors here?
faqs.a: Dry season, roughly November through April, is the comfortable window for pours, coatings, and finish work, and it is also when everyone wants their terrace finished, so contractors book ahead. Summer work is entirely doable with smart sequencing around afternoon rain, though hurricane season requires a site kept storm-ready at all times, which we do as standard practice. The practical advice: start design and permitting months before the season you want to be outside.

faqs.q: How long does a terrace and summer kitchen project take?
faqs.a: Once permits are issued, a full terrace with a summer kitchen typically runs a few months of construction, driven by drainage and structural work up front and stone and equipment installation at the end. Add design and permitting time ahead of that, which varies between the City of Miami and City of Miami Beach. We map the whole sequence in your written scope, so the project has a calendar and not just a hope.

permitting-compliance.h1: A clean file before you close
permitting-compliance.hero_sub: Permit filing, plan review, HVHZ product approvals, inspections, and the open permit a title search just turned up, handled on all six Venetian Islands, in the City of Miami or the City of Miami Beach. Lic. CGC1539072.
permitting-compliance.local_heading: Which city holds your permit file
intro_paragraphs: Six islands, two municipalities, and a century of quiet renovation. The 1930s villas on Di Lido, the postwar houses on Rivo Alto and San Marino, the 1960s and 70s towers on Belle Isle: most of them have had a roof replaced, windows swapped, a kitchen gutted or a terrace enclosed at some point, and not all of it was ever filed. An open or expired permit simply sits in the record until a title search, an appraiser or an insurer goes looking, and on the Venetian Islands that tends to happen a few weeks before a closing.

Which building department you answer to depends on which bridge you cross. Biscayne Island and San Marco Island file with the City of Miami Building Department, through its iBuild and ePlan systems under Miami 21 zoning. San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto and Belle Isle file with the City of Miami Beach through its Civic Access portal, where planning review, floodplain rules and FEMA's substantial-improvement threshold sit on top of the building permit. Whichever city issues the permit, Miami-Dade County stays involved: its Board of Rules and Appeals oversees code administration countywide, county product approvals govern glazing and roofing, and DERM reviews seawall and dock work.

PGX Builders Group is a licensed general contractor, CGC1539072, with 20-plus years in South Florida and more than 150 remodels and additions delivered, all of them permitted and inspected. On the compliance side that means reading the property's permit record before quoting anything, telling you plainly what is open and what finishing it will take, and coordinating the architect, engineer or marine contractor the file genuinely needs. We take over as contractor of record when the original one has long since vanished. A supervisor meets the inspector on the island. Nobody here will promise to make a requirement disappear.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: From an open file to a closed one
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Whether you are planning work on the islands or inherited somebody else's paperwork with the deed, the permit side gets scoped in writing like any other job.

scope_items.name: Inherited open permits
scope_items.desc: We pull the property's permit history, work out exactly what stalled, renew or refile it, and step in as contractor of record when the original one is gone.

scope_items.name: Filed with the right city
scope_items.desc: Applications, drawings and review comments run through City of Miami iBuild or Miami Beach Civic Access depending on your island, so the file starts where it belongs.

scope_items.name: Glass, doors and approvals
scope_items.desc: Windows, doors, shutters and roofing documented with Miami-Dade or state approvals and installed with the anchors and substrate that approval specifies, which is what the inspector reads.

scope_items.name: Inspections called in order
scope_items.desc: Trades staged so each inspection is genuinely ready when it is booked, met on site by a PGX supervisor, with correction notices answered rather than shelved.

scope_items.name: Belle Isle building repairs
scope_items.desc: Concrete, railing, waterproofing and electrical work called for by a recertification, milestone inspection or reserve study, permitted and built alongside your association's engineer.

faqs.q: A title search found an open permit on my Venetian Islands house. What now?
faqs.a: We pull the record first and find where it stopped: a final inspection nobody ever called, an abandoned trade inspection, or work that drifted from the approved drawings. From there the permit is renewed or refiled with the correct city, PGX is named contractor of record if the original contractor is unreachable, and the outstanding inspections are completed. Lenders and title companies want the file clean. Start weeks ahead of your closing date, not days.

faqs.q: Do I file with the City of Miami or the City of Miami Beach?
faqs.a: It depends on the island, and guessing wrong costs time you probably do not have. Biscayne Island and San Marco Island sit inside the City of Miami. San Marino, Di Lido, Rivo Alto and Belle Isle sit inside the City of Miami Beach. Same causeway, same water, two building departments with different portals, different review layers and different local amendments. We work in both regularly and confirm jurisdiction against the address before a single sheet is submitted.

faqs.q: The previous owner enclosed a terrace and swapped windows without permits. Can that be legalized?
faqs.a: Usually, though after the fact is the expensive way to do it. The work has to be documented, brought to current code and inspected, which sometimes means opening finishes so an engineer or inspector can see what is behind them. Windows and doors are the usual sticking point: anything installed on these islands needs a product approval for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, and glass that was never approved for these wind loads generally comes back out.

faqs.q: Does recertification or the condo milestone inspection apply to my Belle Isle building?
faqs.a: If you are in a Belle Isle tower rather than a house, very likely. Miami-Dade's building recertification program, the one everyone still calls the 40-year even though the first inspection now comes sooner, exempts single-family homes and duplexes but not the towers. Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study apply to condominium buildings of three or more habitable stories, which is Belle Plaza, Costa Brava, the Grand Venetian and their neighbors. Your engineer writes the report; we permit and build the repairs it calls for.

faqs.q: How long does permitting take out here, and can you speed it up?
faqs.a: Not in the way people mean by expediting. Nobody legitimately jumps the queue, and a contractor who offers to has told you something useful about how he works. What actually moves a file is a complete, coordinated submittal, review comments answered the week they arrive, and drawings that match the product approvals. Plan in weeks and months rather than days, in either city. Florida also allows private provider review and inspections on qualifying work, and we raise that when it genuinely fits.
